text:
maria: Quick perf thread — noticed p50 latency spike (~25%) when a 30B model is packed with multiple 7B instances on the same GPU. Seems correlated with KV eviction churn and increased memcpy times.
ajay: ugh, saw that in the nightly too. any kernel fallback traces?
sophie: I profiled a few runs. kernel selector is falling back from fused-attn to generic aten path at ~seq_len 1024 for the 30B, which increases workspace alloc churn.
maria: exactly. suspect the allocator lane sizing + workspace rounding causes the 7B instances to fragment the slab and push the 30B's temp buffers to swap.
noah: can you paste the profiler sample? small logs are enough.
sophie: here — short excerpt from perf log: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] model=redwood-30b kernel=fused_attn eligible=false reason=memory_layout_mismatch
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] alloc: requested=1.2GB rounded=1.25GB lane=A workspace_pool=slot_3
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] eviction: kv_evicted=48 shards; memcpy_wait=12ms
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] fallback_path memcpy=9.8ms vs fused 0.9ms
```
ajay: memcpy_wait 12ms is brutal for p50. that matches what we saw.
maria: hypothesis: lane proportional throttling currently uses a static ratio per model size. when mixed with aggressive KV prefetch it ends up stealing workspace from the big model transiently.
ben: idea: introduce a soft-reserve tag for large model primary workspace + prefer kernel variants that accept preallocated workspace instead of allocating per-call. small change in selector table.
sophie: also saw the KV shard policy is LRU across all tenants on the GPU. when many small models issue concurrent prefix lookups, they evict the 30B's KV pages — causing recompute + refill overhead.
noah: thinking of a two-tier KV policy: protected_shard for pinned models (30B) and pooled_shard for bursty small models. low overhead to track by model_id.
majay: @ajay (typo) meant @maria — any perf regression timeline? when did this surface?
maria: started after the allocator change in release v0.38 (workspace rounding to 64MB). before that large model workspaces had contiguous slots.
ajay: maybe revert rounding and instead do "adaptive rounding" based on fragmentation metric. keep current perf benefits for uniform workloads.
sophie: for experiments I ran a synthetic mix: 1x30B + 4x7B with kv_prefetch=enabled. results: p50 260ms -> 330ms with current master; with two-tier kv + soft-reserve it goes to 275ms.
ben: nice. can you share the config snippet you used for the two-tier policy?
sophie: snippet: 
```json
{
  "allocator": { "adaptive_rounding": true, "fragmentation_threshold": 0.12 },
  "workspace": { "soft_reserve_mb": { "30B": 1536 }, "prefer_prealloc": true },
  "kv": { "shard_policy": "two_tier", "protected_pct": 0.2 }
}
```
maria: next actions: 1) bench adaptive_rounding toggle at infra scale, 2) add protected_shard experiment to staging, 3) add kernel selector hint to prefer prealloc-friendly kernels for models with soft_reserve.
noah: i'll spin up instances on the perf cluster and run the mix tests tomorrow morning, assign to perf queue.
infra-bot: perf-job #4523 queued (suite: mixed_models_1x30b_4x7b, owner: noah). ETA ~2h. :robot_face:
ben: also flagging a UX note - expose workspace soft_reserve in the Console as advanced opt for Dedicated customers. ops love knobs.
maria: thanks all. i'll open three small PRs: allocator config toggle, kv two-tier small shim, and selector hint. please review fast. :thumbsup:
ajay: thx — will review the allocator PR.
sophie: I'll post perf numbers back here when infra-bot finishes the run.
